answer: A periodic pulse samples behavior and propagates trust via a ripple across peers; sybils multiplying identities dilute stake per node, so a 51% fake swarm costs the attacker linear bond capital with no discounted bulk rate, while honest participants recover stake after the pulse confirms consistent behavior. Each new agent must route its first transaction through a single verified inlet, staking a bond that scales with claimed reputation. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
